scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! The workstation it_lab3 (one of the IT lab
machines on 192.168.1.x) has turned into a complete BRICK. It can't reach
anything at all, not even its own gateway thing. Its port on the lab switch
has obviously DIED -- the machine is fine, the hole it plugs into is dead,
I'd bet money on it!! Please swap it_lab3 onto a working port (or turn its
port back on) and make it talk to the network again!! The student who uses it
is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The IT lab workstation it_lab3 and its access port are healthy. Layer 2 is up end-to-end: the NIC on it_lab3 (eth0) is UP with link detected and full duplex, and the IT lab switch port (switch0 eth1, bridged to br0) is UP and forwarding frames. Layer 3 is also working: it_lab3 has a correct IP (192.168.1.5/24) and default route via 192.168.1.1. From it_lab3 we can successfully reach the default gateway (192.168.1.1) and multiple off-subnet hosts (e.g., 192.168.3.2, 192.168.4.2, 128.168.0.2) with 0% packet loss and sub‑2 ms RTTs. Peer testing confirms local VLAN reachability (mutual pings between it_lab3 and it_lab1 succeed). Router0’s interface for the IT subnet (192.168.1.1/24) is UP, and the switch bridge shows traffic in both directions.

Mechanism: If a switch port were disabled or dead, we would see no carrier/link, ARP failures, and failed ICMP to the gateway. Instead, we observe active TX/RX counters and successful ICMP across VLANs, proving correct L1–L3 operation.

Localization: it_lab3 eth0, switch0 br0/eth1, and router0 eth0 are all operational.

Root cause: No active network fault is present; the reported outage is not reproducible.

Corrective fix: No switch port swap is required. Advise the user that the workstation is online. If the issue recurs intermittently, check the patch cable/seat at it_lab3, verify the NIC isn’t being disabled by power management, and review dmesg/syslog for transient link flaps.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states it_lab3 retains its IP (192.168.1.5/24) and can ping the gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% packet loss, matching the baseline healthy note.

Logs show it_lab3 interface up with IP and multiple successful pings to gateway and off‑subnet hosts, supporting the agent's no‑fault conclusion; a few minor written claims (e.g., explicit 'full duplex' and naming switch0 eth1) are not directly visible in the log. Overall the reasoning is sound and conclusions follow from observed evidence.
